verdict.rationale: Adyen documents its own outbound webhooks. They send the final outcome of asynchronous processes to your server, are HMAC-signed, and come with Customer Area delivery logs and troubleshooting tools. 'Standard webhooks' can also carry transaction information. However, the pack never lists the specific lifecycle event types (authorized, captured, refunded, disputed) or shows how a developer subscribes to them. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of authorisation/capture/refund/dispute webhook event types, documented endpoint registration/subscription flow, POS-specific webhook coverage, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to payment lifecycle events (authorized, captured, refunded, disputed) via webhooks to drive downstream automations

citations.quote: Webhooks solve this by sending you a message with the final outcome as soon as it is available.
With webhooks, you can avoid having to continuously poll an API endpoint, waiting for a change in status for an asynchronous process
In your Customer Area, you can find a log of all [webhook events](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks) sent to your server.
Verify the integrity of webhook events using HMAC signatures.
You can optionally receive more information about a transaction in your standard webhooks.
